title: One direct-image test transfers affine tensor cohomology vanishing
statement: Let S be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], U an affine open, R = Gamma(U,O_S), and K an object of D(O_S) [def-pc-derived-category]. Let P be any complex of R-modules whose explicit affine sheafification F_U [lem-pc-affine-perfect-module-model] represents the restriction of K on the localized site over U. Derived localizations on S, its localized opens and Spec R are fixed, with the spectrum localization allowed an independent universe. Put j = isoSpec.inv followed by U -> S. For any O_{Spec R}-module sheaf G and integer i, if H^i(K tensor^L j_*G) vanishes in the K-flat-model sense of [def-pc-derived-tensor-cohomology-vanishes], then H^i(Q(tilde P) tensor^L G) vanishes in the same sense on Spec R. No finite Tor dimension, interval bounds, pseudo-coherence or boundedness is assumed.

source.place: Proof of (1), exact restriction and tensor; Tor testing from Tag 08CG; localized affine transport as in Tag 06Z0

proof.text: Let R = Gamma(S,U) and j = isoSpec.inv followed by the open inclusion U -> S. For the given spectrum module sheaf G, take the actual global sheaf F = j_*G. The open-immersion counit identifies j^*F with G (Mathlib Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctorAdjCounitIso). Unpack the assumed degree-i vanishing as a K-flat model C of K and zero degree-i cohomology of C tensor F[0].

Restrict C first to U and then along the affine spectrum isomorphism. Exactness transports the zero homology object. K-flatness is preserved by open restriction and by the spectrum isomorphism. Restriction commutes with total tensor, so after the counit identification this gives zero H^i of the restricted C tensor G[0]. Equivalently one may use the derived tensor restriction comparison and the exact-functor homology comparison to obtain the same vanishing.

Use the affine localized-site derived transport and its comparison with termwise tilde. Apply its inverse to the given representing isomorphism hP, and compose with the localization factorization for restriction. The inverse identities for isoSpec and overEquiv identify the restricted C with Q(tilde P) in the spectrum derived category. The restricted K-flat C, this representing isomorphism, and the zero homology from the preceding step form the witness for the conclusion. These comparisons allow independent localization universes and do not require boundedness.
